<h2>SherlockEQ 0.2.0</h2>

<p>
  The first feature release since 0.1: <strong>Listening Comfort</strong> —
  level-dependent processing that shapes sound only while it needs it,
  instead of permanently re-tuning the curve. Soften a harsh "sss," ease
  shouty midrange, or lift dialogue over a score — each engages when the
  triggering sound is present and relaxes when it's gone. Per ear, zero
  added latency, and the peak limiter stays the ceiling over any boost.
</p>

<h3>Added</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Listening Comfort panel.</strong>
    A new sidebar section with three named, preconfigured processors —
    <em>Speech Presence</em>, <em>Harshness Control</em>, and
    <em>Sibilance Tamer</em>. Each is just an on/off, a Strength slider,
    and a Sensitivity slider, with a live activity meter showing how much
    it's working in the moment. Independent per ear, with the same
    Separate&nbsp;L/R switch the rest of the app uses.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Adaptive, level-independent triggering.</strong>
    Each processor measures its target band against a slow rolling
    average of that band, so it behaves the same on a quiet podcast and a
    loud movie — no SPL calibration required. Sensitivity sets how far
    above that average it reacts; Strength sets how much it does.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Dynamics overlay on the Expert canvas.</strong>
    A new <em>Dynamics</em> layer chip draws each active processor's
    response live, moving under your static EQ curve, so you can watch
    the comfort tools engage against the spectrum in real time.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Changed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Reference Mode and the chain bypass now cover the comfort
    tools.</strong>
    Reference Mode (⌘B / the title-bar toggle) drops the Listening
    Comfort stage along with the rest of the chain, so your A/B is still
    a true comparison against the unprocessed source. A dedicated
    per-stage toggle lets you turn the comfort tools off while keeping
    your EQ, headphone correction, and notch active.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Fixed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Menu-bar popover lingered behind the main window.</strong>
    Opening the full app from the popover now closes the popover instead
    of leaving it floating in front of the window.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not
  diagnose, treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus,
  or disability. The Listening Comfort tools shape audio for comfort and
  clarity — they are not a hearing aid. For concerns about your hearing,
  consult a doctor, audiologist, or licensed healthcare professional.
</p>
